about: Hand-marked passages for the style checks and the overly descriptive check (piece Q.1). Original text written for the benchmark. Each mark names a kind of check, a snippet of the passage, and whether a flag there would be RIGHT (flag: true, a real weakness an editor would want changed) or WRONG (flag: false, a deliberate choice: a character's voice, a fragment for effect, a passive that fits). The passages are fully marked: a flag of a kind that matches no mark of that kind counts as wrong. Marks are a draft by the session that built Q.1, for the writer to review. A mark covers every occurrence of its snippet in the passage. Passages with a "scores" list (added in P.2a for transitions, pronouns, alliteration and acronyms) are fully marked only for those kinds and are scored only on them, so the earlier checks' numbers do not move.
status: draft — to be reviewed by the writer

passages.text: The door was kicked open before anyone could move. Glass was thrown across the floor, and Mara was dragged into the hall.

marks.why: Action scene: who kicked it is the point.
Hides the actor in a fight.
Mara should be acted on by someone named.
Plain action; its trouble is the passive.

passages.text: Tobin was born in a fishing town on the north coast. The harbour wall was built before the war, and nobody remembered by whom.

marks.why: The natural way to say it.
The builder is unknown, and the sentence says so.

passages.text: She shouted loudly for the dog. He whispered quietly that it was gone, and she sighed sadly.

marks.why: 'Gone' is an adjective here, not a passive.

passages.text: She was barely awake when the phone rang. He nearly dropped the cup, and the line went dead almost immediately.

marks.why: Changes the meaning; cannot be cut.
Changes the meaning; cannot be cut.
States a fact, not a feeling.

passages.text: It was very cold on the pier and really dark beyond the lamps. The water was extremely still.

marks.why: Weak; 'glassy' or a detail would do.

marks.text: It was very cold on the pier
It was very cold on the pier
marks.why: Tells the cold and the dark.
Tells; a detail would show it.

passages.text: "I'm really sorry," Ilse said. "Truly. I just didn't think you'd come."

marks.why: Her voice, and a deliberate fragment.

passages.text: In order to reach the boat in time, he made a decision to run. Mara nodded her head and followed.

marks.why: Its trouble is the wordy phrases.

passages.text: He began to run the moment the shot rang out. Later, as the mourners left the churchyard, the snow began to fall.

marks.why: A gradual beginning is the point.

passages.text: At the end of the day, the plan fell apart all of a sudden, and they escaped in the nick of time.

marks.text: At the end of the day
At the end of the day

passages.text: "Better late than never," Gran said, as she said every Sunday when Tobin came through the door.

marks.why: 'as she said every Sunday' stresses the habit.

passages.text: He opened the drawer. He took out the letter. He read it twice. He put it back and closed the drawer.

marks.why: Bookending the same object is deliberate.

passages.text: We searched the harbour. We searched the cliffs above it. We searched until the tide came in and there was nowhere left to look.
The light from the lamp spilled over the table, and the lamp's light caught the edge of the knife Mara had left there.
Nothing moved on the moor. Nothing breathed. Nothing, for a long while, but the wind.

When they finally reached the station after walking for what felt like hours through the rain and the mud and the dark lanes that all looked the same to Tobin, who had never been good with directions, the last train had already gone.

marks.why: Buries the point at the end.
Carries the sense of a long wait.
Its trouble is length, already flagged.
Hard to follow in one breath.

passages.text: She ran past the boats and the nets and the old ice house, past the chapel and the fish market and the bakery with its lights still on, and did not stop until the road ran out.

marks.why: The run-on rhythm is the running.

passages.text: The administrative reorganisation necessitated considerable reconsideration of institutional responsibilities and organisational accountability.
It was the one that he had been thinking of when he was out in the boat with them all on that night.
"Ain't nobody coming," Jory said. "Not tonight. Not ever. You hear?"
The room was almost too dark to see. She felt very angry about the letter.

marks.text: The room was almost too dark
marks.why: Tells; show what she can't see.

marks.text: The room was almost too dark
marks.why: Its trouble is that it tells.

passages.text: Rain needled the window. Mara counted the drips from the broken gutter and lost count at forty.
The ferry came in late, heavy with cattle and wet sacks of grain. Tobin took the rope from the deckhand and made it fast, and for a moment neither of them spoke.
"I was told to wait here," he said, and he sat down on the step.

marks.why: Natural speech; he doesn't know who.

passages.text: "Get out," she said angrily. He left without a word.

Mara opened the door to the yard. She looked out at the rain. He came up behind her with the lamp. She took it from him. They stood there for a long time without speaking. It was Tobin who moved first.

marks.why: Four pronoun openings in a row; the paragraph loses its shape.

passages.text: Tobin found his brother at the harbour. He told him that he would meet him at his house after he had eaten, and walked off before either of them could argue.

marks.text: He told him that he would meet him at his house after he
marks.why: Two men, six he-forms: the reader can't tell who goes where.

passages.text: "I know. I said so. I meant it. You heard me," Ilse said, and turned back to the sink.

marks.why: A character's speech; her rhythm, not the narrator's.

passages.text: The town had one road and one bridge over the river. The bridge had a toll house at the north end. A man named Pell kept the toll house for thirty years. Pell wrote every cart and every coin in a ledger. The ledger lived on a shelf above the stove. Nobody in the town ever asked to read it. The river took the bridge in the spring flood of that year.

marks.why: Seven flat statements; nothing tells the reader how they connect, or that the last one is the turn.

passages.text: The ferry was late again, so Tobin waited on the wall. When it came at last, the deck was crowded with cattle. He found a place by the rail, but the smell drove him inside. There the benches were wet. Still, it was warmer, and he slept until the engines changed note. Then he went up to watch the town come out of the mist.

Her coat hung on the hook by the door. Her boots stood under it with the laces tucked in. A cup sat upside down on the draining board. The calendar on the wall showed the month she died. The radio on the sill was tuned to the shipping forecast. Her reading glasses lay folded on the open book.

marks.text: Her coat hung on the hook
marks.why: An inventory of a dead woman's kitchen; the missing links are the point.

passages.text: She put the plastic plates on the porch and went back for the bread. Gran was asleep in the chair with the cat on her knee.

marks.why: An accidental tongue-twister in plain narration.

passages.text: Beyond the harbour wall the sea lay silver, slow and sliding, and the boats came home one by one with their lamps lit.

marks.why: Lyrical on purpose: the sound is the sea.

passages.text: The NTSB team arrived at noon. Nobody had told Ruiz they were coming, and the lead investigator made it clear he did not want her near his wreckage.

marks.why: Many readers won't know it; the full name is needed once.

passages.text: The FDR was found in the mud by the fence. Okafor wanted the F.D.R. sent to the lab before dark, and Ruiz carried the FDR to the van herself.

marks.why: Written two ways in one passage.
The form used most; it is the other one to change.

passages.text: The Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) sent two inspectors from Farnborough. By evening the AAIB had taken over the hangar, and nobody else was allowed inside.

marks.why: Spelled out at first use, as it should be.

passages.text: "STOP!" Ruiz shouted. "Get BACK from the edge!" The boy froze with one foot on the rail.
